sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi, and this is The Daily.

sentences.en: When Donald Trump won the presidency in 2016, it prompted an outpouring of protests, particularly by women, a movement that came to be known as the resistance.
sentences.zh: 当唐纳德·特朗普在2016年赢得总统大选时，引发了大规模的抗议，尤其是女性的抗议，这场运动后来被称为“抵抗运动”。

sentences.en: For the past two weeks, Daily producer Lindsay Garrison has been talking to people who were part of that movement, asking them what they're doing after Trump's win this time.
sentences.zh: 在过去两周里，《每日新闻》的制片人琳赛·加里森一直在与参与过那场运动的人们交谈，询问他们在特朗普这次胜选后打算做什么。

sentences.en: Today, what they said about the state of the resistance in the next Trump era.
sentences.zh: 今天，他们讲述了在下一个特朗普时代，“抵抗运动”的现状。

sentences.zh: 大选几天后，我给瓦妮莎·鲁贝尔打了电话。

sentences.zh: 她住在南加州沙漠里的一片五英亩的土地上。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.zh: 那是什么声音？

sentences.zh: 它现在正在发出声音。

sentences.zh: 你听到的背景音。

sentences.en: You're hearing Byron, who is a parrot.

sentences.zh: 哦，真的吗？

sentences.en: We run a animal sanctuary.
sentences.zh: 我们经营着一个动物庇护所。

sentences.en: Well, actually, it's a sanctuary for humans and animals.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其实，这是一个人类和动物的庇护所。

sentences.en: And we have a ton of different kinds of animals.
sentences.zh: 我们有各种各样的动物。

sentences.en: So, there are like emus roaming around.
sentences.zh: 比如有鸸鹋在到处走动。

sentences.en: And then we have a ton of dogs and pigs and we have a zebra.
sentences.zh: 还有很多狗、猪，我们甚至还有一匹斑马。

sentences.en: That's pretty intense.
sentences.zh: 那真是太震撼了。

sentences.en: It is intense.
sentences.zh: 确实很震撼。

sentences.zh: 这是一种非常不同的生活。

sentences.en: in New York City, running a company in the music industry, and thought the country was about to elect its first woman president.
sentences.zh: 纽约市，经营着一家音乐行业的公司，并以为国家即将选出第一位女总统。

sentences.en: I had been watching the election with friends.
sentences.zh: 我当时和朋友们一起看大选。

sentences.en: And there was already a party planned in Brooklyn, and we had expected to go roll out to that party and celebrate with everyone.
sentences.zh: 布鲁克林已经计划好了一场派对，我们本打算去那场派对和大家一起庆祝。

sentences.en: And when things started going south, I just kept saying, no, no, no, no, no, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 当情况开始恶化时，我一直说，不，不，不，不，不，不，不，不。

sentences.en: No, this can't happen.
sentences.zh: 不，这不可能发生。

sentences.en: This is no way.
sentences.zh: 这绝不可能。

sentences.en: There's no way.
sentences.zh: 没可能的。

sentences.en: You know, it felt like there had been a death in the room, you know, like someone had died.
sentences.zh: 你知道，感觉就像房间里有人去世了一样，你知道，就像有人死了。

sentences.en: And that feeling, there was nothing like it.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉，前所未有。

sentences.en: I could not believe that that was the world we are living in.
sentences.zh: 我无法相信这就是我们生活的世界。

sentences.en: And I could not believe someone who had been accused of rape and sexual harassment and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 我也无法相信，一个被指控强奸、性骚扰等等的人。

sentences.en: People would rather have that person in the White House.
sentences.zh: 人们竟然宁愿让这样的人入主白宫。

sentences.en: And I really do think it was because she was a woman.
sentences.zh: 我真的认为这是因为她是个女人。

sentences.en: And then I woke up the next day and I was like, well, either I'm going to lay down and die or I'm going to do something about this.
sentences.zh: 第二天醒来时，我想，要么我就躺平等死，要么我就得为此做点什么。

sentences.en: And that anger was very motivating.
sentences.zh: 那种愤怒非常有动力。

sentences.en: So, you know, women everywhere were so incredibly upset and everyone gathered on one Facebook page.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，各地的女性都极其愤怒，大家都在一个Facebook页面上聚集起来。

sentences.en: First, it started just a Facebook group.
sentences.zh: 起初，它只是一个Facebook群组。

sentences.en: It started so small.
sentences.zh: 开始时规模很小。

sentences.en: It would be like 20 members starting a Facebook group.
sentences.zh: 就像20个成员发起的一个Facebook群组。

sentences.en: And I became one of the leaders of that page.
sentences.zh: 我成了那个页面的领导者之一。

sentences.en: And what I even call women's march at firSt.
sentences.zh: 我甚至在最初称之为“女性大游行”。

sentences.en: And I started pulling people in to organize who I knew could make this happen.
sentences.zh: 我开始拉拢那些我知道能促成此事的人来组织活动。

sentences.en: At that time, they were looking for leadership positions.
sentences.zh: 那时，他们正在寻找领导职位。

sentences.en: And I felt like, OK, this is what I served.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，好吧，这就是我的使命。

sentences.en: This is the oath I took to this country.
sentences.zh: 这就是我对这个国家宣下的誓言。

sentences.en: T.
sentences.zh: T。

sentences.en: Marie Hannibal served in the Marine Corps for 20 years.
sentences.zh: 玛丽·汉尼拔在海军陆战队服役了20年。

sentences.en: She's a retired gunnery sergeant.
sentences.zh: 她是一位退役的炮术军士。

sentences.en: I didn't go into combat for nothing.
sentences.zh: 我参军不是为了白白浪费。

sentences.en: And now I'm in a space where I feel like our rights are being taken away, even here on the homeland.
sentences.zh: 现在我所处的空间让我觉得我们的权利正在被剥夺，即使是在我们的国土上。

sentences.en: So what was the purpose of my military service?
sentences.zh: 那么我服兵役的目的是什么呢？

sentences.en: I felt like I had to do something.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我必须做点什么。

sentences.en: I think at that time, for me, it was really about the women's rights.
sentences.zh: 我想当时对我来说，这真的是关于女性权利。

sentences.en: And I'm a Black woman, so not just the veteran, the Black woman in me, the woman in me, prior to coming into the Marine Corps, I was that 17-year-old who had an abortion.
sentences.zh: 我是个黑人女性，所以不仅仅是退伍军人，我内心里的黑人女性，我内心里的女性，在加入海军陆战队之前，我就是那个17岁时堕过胎的孩子。

sentences.en: I was that child in the abortion clinic.
sentences.zh: 我就是那个在堕胎诊所里的孩子。

sentences.en: That was me.
sentences.zh: 那就是我。

sentences.en: That's my story.
sentences.zh: 那是我的故事。

sentences.en: So for me, it was more so the women's rights, if that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，更多的是关于女性权利，如果这说得通的话。

sentences.en: So you thought under a Trump administration, there was a real possibility that abortion access could be denied?
sentences.zh: 所以你认为在特朗普政府下，堕胎渠道真的有可能被拒绝？

sentences.en: Oh, I knew it.
sentences.zh: 哦，我知道。

sentences.en: I knew it.
sentences.zh: 我早就知道。

sentences.en: That's all he pushed.
sentences.zh: 他所推崇的就只有这些。

sentences.en: That's all he talked about.
sentences.zh: 他谈论的也只有这些。

sentences.en: And so let's talk about these things now so that it doesn't happen.
sentences.zh: 所以现在让我们谈谈这些事情，这样它就不会发生。

sentences.en: Let's make sure we're advocating for these things now so that, you know, it won't happen.
sentences.zh: 让我们确保现在就为这些事情进行倡导，这样，你知道，它就不会发生。

sentences.en: And then I'm getting word of, OK, maybe we can proteSt.
sentences.zh: 然后我得到消息说，好吧，也许我们可以抗议。

sentences.en: OK, maybe we should proteSt.
sentences.zh: 好吧，也许我们应该抗议。

sentences.en: Now what?
sentences.zh: 现在怎么办？

sentences.en: And then from there, I started calling people that I knew in different states to kind of help me, because this was definitely new to my little house.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，我开始打电话给我认识的不同州的人来帮我，因为这对我这个小家庭来说绝对是新鲜事。

sentences.en: And lo and behold, women veterans started stepping up, and it just grew legs.
sentences.zh: 果不其然，女性退伍军人开始站出来，事情就这样发展起来了。

sentences.en: It just grew into something I don't think anyone foresaw.
sentences.zh: 它发展成了我认为没人预见到的样子。

sentences.en: You know, I was on Facebook, and I started seeing all the posts because it just had started going viral.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我在Facebook上，开始看到所有的帖子，因为它已经开始病毒式传播了。

sentences.en: What is this?
sentences.zh: 这是什么？

sentences.en: What is this march?
sentences.zh: 这是什么游行？

sentences.en: And when I got the call to action, you know, we're going to march, I was just like, wow, I know what to do with this.
sentences.zh: 当我接到行动号召时，你知道，我们要去游行，我当时就想，哇，我知道该怎么做了。

sentences.en: And I started Women's March Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 我发起了宾夕法尼亚州的女性大游行。

sentences.en: I'm down to mobilize my state of South Carolina.
sentences.zh: 我准备动员我的南卡罗来纳州。

sentences.en: I'm going to take on getting Rhode Island together.
sentences.zh: 我要负责把罗德岛组织起来。

sentences.en: At some point, it just took a life of its own.
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，它有了自己的生命力。

sentences.en: It was like this way, particularly amongst women, but also with our male allies, because we don't do this without our male allies.
sentences.zh: 这是一种方式，特别是在女性中间，但也包括我们的男性盟友，因为没有我们的男性盟友，我们做不到这一点。

sentences.en: People felt like they had to try and do something about this.
sentences.zh: 人们觉得他们必须尝试为此做点什么。

sentences.en: People are indignant.
sentences.zh: 人们感到愤慨。

sentences.en: People are furious.
sentences.zh: 人们感到愤怒。

sentences.en: I think it was rage.
sentences.zh: 我认为那是狂怒。

sentences.en: It was just absolute rage.
sentences.zh: 那是绝对的狂怒。

sentences.en: It was just a sense of fire.
sentences.zh: 那是一种火一样的感觉。

sentences.en: Like, everybody was ready.
sentences.zh: 就像，每个人都准备好了。

sentences.en: It was that, we ride at midnight type of feel.
sentences.zh: 那是一种“我们午夜出征”的感觉。

sentences.en: Failure wasn't an option, right?
sentences.zh: 失败不是选项，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, you just, I don't know, it's just like a bulldozer, and we were going to get this done.
sentences.zh: 就像，你只是，我不知道，就像推土机一样，我们要把这件事做成。

sentences.en: On the day of the march, you know, I stood on that stage, and I looked out, you know, and I had been kind of critical of the Pussyhat, because that wasn't, like, directly us.
sentences.zh: 在游行那天，你知道，我站在那个舞台上，我向外望去，你知道，我之前对“猫耳帽”持批评态度，因为那不是直接代表我们。

sentences.en: That was the Pussyhat Project.
sentences.zh: 那是“猫耳帽计划”。

sentences.en: And I had been like, oh, well, that's, you know, a pink hat.
sentences.zh: 我当时说，哦，好吧，那只是，你知道，一顶粉色的帽子。

sentences.en: That's kind of lame.
sentences.zh: 那有点逊。

sentences.en: And, like, people felt that it wasn't inclusive, because not all pussies are pink.
sentences.zh: 而且，人们觉得它不具包容性，因为并不是所有的猫咪都是粉色的。

sentences.en: You know, it became a little contentious.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这变得有点争议。

sentences.en: And, but when I got on, you know, when I stood on the stage as people came in, it was like an absolute wave of pink coming over, you know, Capitol Hill.
sentences.zh: 但是当我上去时，你知道，当我站在舞台上看着人们进来时，那就像一股绝对的粉色浪潮涌向，你知道，国会山。

sentences.en: It was astonishing.
sentences.zh: 太令人震惊了。

sentences.en: I mean, just imagine looking out at miles and miles and miles of people.
sentences.zh: 我是说，试想一下，放眼望去是绵延数英里的人群。

sentences.en: It was amazing.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: It was just amazing just to see.
sentences.zh: 看到这一切真是太棒了。

sentences.en: Just to see.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是看到。

sentences.en: Did it feel like the country was kind of on your side?
sentences.zh: 感觉国家好像站在你这边吗？

sentences.en: I mean, it felt good to be able to say, okay, most Americans feel that way.
sentences.zh: 我是说，能说出“好吧，大多数美国人都有这种感觉”让人感觉很好。

sentences.en: So I would say, yeah, it feels good to feel like, okay, for the most part, when I meet somebody else, I can still hold my head up high.
sentences.zh: 所以我可以说，是的，感觉很好，觉得好吧，在大多数情况下，当我遇到别人时，我仍然可以昂首挺胸。

sentences.en: It was just, it was otherworldly.
sentences.zh: 那简直是，那简直是超凡脱俗。

sentences.en: It was sublime.
sentences.zh: 那太崇高了。

sentences.en: And I stood on the stage that day, and I thought, like, this is absolutely incredible.
sentences.zh: 那天我站在舞台上，我想，这简直太不可思议了。

sentences.en: But we need to take this energy and harness it and create a movement.
sentences.zh: 但我们需要利用这种能量，驾驭它，并创造一场运动。

sentences.en: This is just the beginning.
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是个开始。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜露。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我编写《纽约时报》游戏中的拼图游戏《Connections》。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基，我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你们刚才听到的人们制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 立即开始游戏。

sentences.en: This is just the beginning.
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是个开始。

sentences.en: We need to take this energy and harness it.
sentences.zh: 我们需要利用这种能量，并驾驭它。

sentences.en: And so the question is, what does that look like?
sentences.zh: 所以问题是，那会是什么样子？

sentences.en: And I think, ultimately, what it looked like was, you know, different groups forming different organizations to ensure that Trump did not have a second term.
sentences.zh: 我认为，归根结底，那样子就是，你知道，不同的群体组建了不同的组织，以确保特朗普不会有第二个任期。

sentences.en: After the Women's March, a number of women's rights organizations sprouted up across the nation.
sentences.zh: 妇女大游行之后，全国各地涌现出许多妇女权利组织。

sentences.en: March On was one of those.
sentences.zh: “March On”就是其中之一。

sentences.en: One of those was March On, a nonprofit that Vanessa ran.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是“March On”，一个由凡妮莎运营的非营利组织。

sentences.en: Women Win was basically one of our slogans.
sentences.zh: “女性获胜”基本上是我们的口号之一。

sentences.en: Part of the work they did was also raise money and campaign for women running for office.
sentences.zh: 她们所做的工作还包括筹款，并为竞选公职的女性开展竞选活动。

sentences.en: And we were successful.
sentences.zh: 我们成功了。

sentences.en: And two years later, women got into office in record numbers in the 2018 midterm elections.
sentences.zh: 两年后，在2018年的中期选举中，女性当选公职的人数创下了历史新高。

sentences.en: Women running and women winning was a direct result of the Women's March.
sentences.zh: 女性参选并获胜是妇女大游行的直接成果。

sentences.en: And in 2020, when Trump lost the election to Joe Biden, it felt like a triumph to activists.
sentences.zh: 2020年，当特朗普在选举中输给乔·拜登时，这对活动人士来说感觉像是一场胜利。

sentences.en: Things were swinging back in the right direction.
sentences.zh: 事情正在向正确的方向回转。

sentences.en: When, you know, Biden stepped down.
sentences.zh: 当，你知道，拜登退选时。

sentences.en: And then this year, when Kamala Harris was announced as the new Democratic nominee for president.
sentences.zh: 然后今年，当卡玛拉·哈里斯被宣布为新的民主党总统候选人时。

sentences.en: For many of the Women's March organizers, the feeling was electric.
sentences.zh: 对于许多妇女大游行的组织者来说，那种感觉令人振奋。

sentences.en: It was this burst of hope and movement again and energy.
sentences.zh: 那是一种希望、运动和能量的再次迸发。

sentences.en: And I felt that deeply.
sentences.zh: 我对此感同身受。

sentences.en: Yeah, it gave us all hope again.
sentences.zh: 是的，它让我们再次看到了希望。

sentences.en: The outcome of this election is not what we wanted.
sentences.zh: 这次选举的结果不是我们想要的。

sentences.en: Not what we fought for.
sentences.zh: 不是我们为之奋斗的结果。

sentences.en: Not what we voted for.
sentences.zh: 不是我们投票支持的结果。

sentences.en: But hear me when I say.
sentences.zh: 但请听我说。

sentences.en: Hear me when I say.
sentences.zh: 请听我说。

sentences.en: The light of America's promise will always burn bright.
sentences.zh: 美国承诺之光将永远闪耀。

sentences.en: So it was, it felt again like, like there had been a death.
sentences.zh: 所以当时，感觉就像，就像发生了一场死亡一样。

sentences.en: And I was sitting with, you know, a couple other women.
sentences.zh: 我当时和，你知道，另外几个女人坐在一起。

sentences.en: And it was just like, how has this happened again?
sentences.zh: 当时的感觉就是，怎么会再次发生这种事？

sentences.en: How has this happened again?
sentences.zh: 怎么会再次发生这种事？

sentences.en: How is this the world we live in?
sentences.zh: 这就是我们生活的世界吗？

sentences.en: Like, why would we ever go back to what happened?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们要回到过去发生的事情上？

sentences.en: We saw what happened.
sentences.zh: 我们都看到了发生了什么。

sentences.en: I was so extremely hopeful.
sentences.zh: 我当时非常充满希望。

sentences.en: I even hosted a watch party for other women veterans here.
sentences.zh: 我甚至还在这里为其他女性退伍军人举办了观选派对。

sentences.en: And we decked out the whole basement, put up little decorations, everything.
sentences.zh: 我们把整个地下室都装饰了一番，挂上了小装饰品，什么都有。

sentences.en: And I hosted a watch party in 2016.
sentences.zh: 我在2016年也举办过观选派对。

sentences.en: And this year, it felt the same way.
sentences.zh: 今年，感觉是一样的。

sentences.en: Now that night during Hillary's, I cried.
sentences.zh: 希拉里那晚，我哭了。

sentences.en: This year, I did not cry.
sentences.zh: 今年，我没有哭。

sentences.en: There was no tears.
sentences.zh: 没有眼泪。

sentences.en: But I was so very disappointed.
sentences.zh: 但我非常失望。

sentences.en: So we wound up, I think we closed up shop at about 11.30.
sentences.zh: 所以我们最后，我想我们在11点半左右收摊了。

sentences.en: They left this house so sad.
sentences.zh: 她们离开这所房子时非常难过。

sentences.en: So very sad.
sentences.zh: 非常难过。

sentences.en: But yeah, it was, it didn't hit me as bad.
sentences.zh: 但确实，它，它没有对我造成那么大的打击。

sentences.en: Because maybe I mentally prepared for it.
sentences.zh: 也许是因为我在心理上做好了准备。

sentences.en: Maybe I kind of knew it.
sentences.zh: 也许我多少预料到了。

sentences.en: But at the end of the day, women are still looked at as not worthy.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，女性仍然被认为是不够格的。

sentences.en: No matter what their resumes look like.
sentences.zh: 无论她们的简历看起来如何。

sentences.en: No matter how many degrees, it does not matter.
sentences.zh: 无论有多少学位，都没用。

sentences.en: So I think this year, I was just defeated in knowing that, yep, we really have not progressed.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为今年，我只是感到挫败，因为我知道，是的，我们真的没有进步。

sentences.en: You know, you said in 2016, there was a fire.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你说2016年的时候，有一团火。

sentences.en: There was a fire.
sentences.zh: 有一团火。

sentences.en: There was a fire.
sentences.zh: 有一团火。

sentences.en: I feel like this year, I feel like this year, I feel like there is a defeat.
sentences.zh: 我觉得今年，我觉得今年，我觉得有一种挫败感。

sentences.en: I feel like before there was hope.
sentences.zh: 我觉得以前还有希望。

sentences.en: And now, it feels very dark.
sentences.zh: 而现在，感觉非常黑暗。

sentences.en: We were all stunned.
sentences.zh: 我们都惊呆了。

sentences.en: I mean, the first time around, we were stunned.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，第一次的时候，我们惊呆了。

sentences.en: Now, it's like people are catatonic.
sentences.zh: 现在，人们就像是处于紧张性精神症状态。

sentences.en: I feel like 2016, we were mad as hell.
sentences.zh: 我觉得2016年，我们愤怒到了极点。

sentences.en: Am I saying we're not mad as hell now?
sentences.zh: 我是说我们现在不愤怒吗？

sentences.en: So I felt like this time was more as a slap in the face.
sentences.zh: 所以我感觉这次更像是一记耳光。

sentences.en: And more particularly for Black women.
sentences.zh: 尤其是对黑人女性而言。

sentences.en: Because the first time, and I can say my military background, has allowed me to see up close and personal how people felt about Hillary Clinton.
sentences.zh: 因为第一次，我可以以我的军事背景来说，让我近距离地看到了人们对希拉里·克林顿的真实感受。

sentences.en: And these potential emails and the mistrust they had of her.
sentences.zh: 还有那些潜在的邮件门，以及他们对她的不信任。

sentences.en: But now, it's somebody, now you didn't have any kind of conspiracy or email gate to contend with.
sentences.zh: 但现在，是另一个人，现在你没有任何阴谋或邮件门可以抗衡了。

sentences.en: So now, what's your excuse?
sentences.zh: 那么现在，你的借口是什么？

sentences.en: And people gave the damnedest excuse from, I just don't know enough about her.
sentences.zh: 人们给出了最离谱的借口，从“我对她了解不够”。

sentences.en: To nobody in Oakland really likes her.
sentences.zh: 到“奥克兰没人真正喜欢她”。

sentences.en: To she's locking up our own people.
sentences.zh: 再到“她把我们自己人关进监狱”。

sentences.en: So, it was such a mirage of excuses.
sentences.zh: 所以，那是一堆借口的幻象。

sentences.en: That tells you, in a nutshell, it really wasn't about any of those things.
sentences.zh: 这简而言之告诉你，这根本不是关于那些事情中的任何一件。

sentences.en: So, this will hurt a little bit more.
sentences.zh: 所以，这次会更痛一点。

sentences.en: America did what America did.
sentences.zh: 美国做了美国会做的事。

sentences.en: And so, what do you do with that?
sentences.zh: 那么，你对此能做什么呢？

sentences.en: I mean, what do you do with that?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你对此能做什么呢？

sentences.en: My daughter, my youngest is 20 and she voted for the first time this year.
sentences.zh: 我的女儿，最小的那个20岁，她今年第一次投票。

sentences.en: And the first thing I got back from my youngest was, I'm literally sick right now.
sentences.zh: 我从她那里得到的第一反应是，我现在真的感到恶心。

sentences.en: Like, physically sick.
sentences.zh: 就像，身体上的恶心。

sentences.en: Like, how did this happen twice, Mom?
sentences.zh: 就像，妈妈，这怎么会发生两次？

sentences.en: Like, Mom, what do we do next?
sentences.zh: 就像，妈妈，我们接下来该怎么办？

sentences.en: I have no idea.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: So many people have asked me, are we protesting?
sentences.zh: 很多人问我，我们要抗议吗？

sentences.en: What are we doing to put me in, coach?
sentences.zh: 我们要怎么做才能让我参与进来，教练？

sentences.en: But I don't know what to put them into.
sentences.zh: 但我不知道该让他们参与什么。

sentences.en: I don't even know if I want to get back out there and proteSt.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不知道我是否还想出去抗议。

sentences.en: And why don't you know whether you'd want to get out there and protest again this time?
sentences.zh: 为什么你不知道这次是否还想出去抗议？

sentences.en: Because what did I change the first time?
sentences.zh: 因为我第一次改变了什么吗？

sentences.en: I don't know if I can really say we achieved a goal.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我是否真的能说我们实现了目标。

sentences.en: We may have slowed some things down.
sentences.zh: 我们可能减缓了一些事情。

sentences.en: But I don't know if he really changed history.
sentences.zh: 但我不知道我们是否真的改变了历史。

sentences.en: I don't know if, had we not done that, would that have changed the trajectory of what happened during his presidency?
sentences.zh: 我不知道，如果我们没那样做，会不会改变他总统任期内发生的事情的轨迹？

sentences.en: Would it have been worse?
sentences.zh: 会更糟吗？

sentences.en: So those are questions I kind of ask myself.
sentences.zh: 所以这些是我会问自己的问题。

sentences.en: But did we really accomplish things?
sentences.zh: 但我们真的完成了什么吗？

sentences.en: I honestly don't know.
sentences.zh: 我真的不知道。

sentences.en: And I'm just tired.
sentences.zh: 而且我只是累了。

sentences.en: I got to ask myself, what is protesting?
sentences.zh: 我得问自己，抗议是什么？

sentences.en: What is putting on that cape again and getting my big old blowhorn out again?
sentences.zh: 再次披上那件斗篷，再次拿出我那大喇叭又是什么？

sentences.en: What is that going to do for us this time around?
sentences.zh: 这次那对我们有什么用？

sentences.en: When it did nothing the first time.
sentences.zh: 第一次的时候它什么都没做到。

sentences.en: I really believed that protest was the way to affect change.
sentences.zh: 我曾经真心相信抗议是影响变革的方式。

sentences.en: I mean, I got into Moms Demand Action really active in that.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我加入了“妈妈要求行动”，在里面非常活跃。

sentences.en: For, you know, responsible gun ownership.
sentences.zh: 为了，你知道，负责任的枪支所有权。

sentences.en: And I was there protesting for the Kavanaugh hearings.
sentences.zh: 我在卡瓦诺听证会时也在那里抗议。

sentences.en: And guess what?
sentences.zh: 你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: It still all happened, right?
sentences.zh: 这一切还是发生了，对吧？

sentences.en: Kavanaugh still got election.
sentences.zh: 卡瓦诺还是当选了。

sentences.en: Kids are still getting killed in schools.
sentences.zh: 孩子们还是在学校里被杀害。

sentences.en: Roe versus Wade still got reversed.
sentences.zh: 罗诉韦德案还是被推翻了。

sentences.en: Here we are, eight years later.
sentences.zh: 八年后的今天，我们在这里。

sentences.en: And not only did Trump win, but he won the popular vote.
sentences.zh: 不仅特朗普赢了，而且他赢得了普选票。

sentences.en: America spoke.
sentences.zh: 美国发声了。

sentences.en: And he won.
sentences.zh: 他赢了。

sentences.en: I mourned for the America that I thought I knew.
sentences.zh: 我为我以为我了解的那个美国哀悼。

sentences.en: I thought our country wanted different things than him.
sentences.zh: 我以为我们的国家想要的东西和他不一样。

sentences.en: But by a free and fair election, this is what they want.
sentences.zh: 但通过一场自由公正的选举，这就是他们想要的。

sentences.en: Whereas before, we can say we were the majority.
sentences.zh: 而以前，我们可以说我们是多数派。

sentences.en: This is not what the country wants.
sentences.zh: 这不是国家想要的。

sentences.en: And we will stand against it.
sentences.zh: 我们将站出来反对它。

sentences.en: We don't have that mandate this time around.
sentences.zh: 这次我们没有那个授权了。

sentences.en: And at this point, fighting this administration is fighting a democratic election.
sentences.zh: 在这一点上，对抗这届政府就是对抗一场民主选举。

sentences.en: Honestly, my first reaction was, you know what, America?
sentences.zh: 老实说，我的第一反应是，你知道吗，美国？

sentences.en: Pardon my French, but fuck it.
sentences.zh: 请原谅我的粗鲁，但去他妈的吧。

sentences.en: If that's how you feel about it, have it, America.
sentences.zh: 如果这就是你的感受，那就拿去吧，美国。

sentences.en: You voted for this.
sentences.zh: 这是你投票选出来的。

sentences.en: Buckle up.
sentences.zh: 系好安全带吧。

sentences.en: It's going to get bad.
sentences.zh: 情况会变得很糟。

sentences.en: And I'm going to say I told you so.
sentences.zh: 到时候我会说我早就告诉过你了。

sentences.en: Would you consider marching again?
sentences.zh: 你会考虑再次游行吗？

sentences.en: Is there talk about marching?
sentences.zh: 有关于游行的讨论吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, and it's not going over real well.
sentences.zh: 有，而且进展得不太顺利。

sentences.en: I know Women's March is planning a march on January 18th.
sentences.zh: 我知道妇女大游行计划在1月18日举行游行。

sentences.en: They're saying it's the people's march.
sentences.zh: 她们说这是人民的游行。

sentences.en: Well, you know what?
sentences.zh: 好吧，你知道吗？

sentences.en: In my mind, the people voted for Trump.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，人民投票给了特朗普。

sentences.en: When I watched Kamala Harris' concession station, people were saying, like, how inspiring it was.
sentences.zh: 当我观看卡玛拉·哈里斯的败选演讲时，人们说，这有多鼓舞人心。

sentences.en: Don't ever give up because she says that.
sentences.zh: 永远不要放弃，因为她这么说。

sentences.en: I'm like, no, this is who I don't.
sentences.zh: 我心想，不，这就是我不想做的。

sentences.en: No, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不，不。

sentences.en: At a certain point, no, you have to give up.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，不，你必须放弃。

sentences.en: Like, I don't have the energy or any battery left in me to do anything other than to play for myself.
sentences.zh: 就像，我没有精力或任何电池留给我去做除了为自己而活之外的任何事情。

sentences.en: And to answer your question for me personally, no.
sentences.zh: 回答你关于我个人的问题，不。

sentences.en: I don't know any organizer from the original Women's March that thinks marching right now is a good idea.
sentences.zh: 我不认识任何最初妇女大游行的组织者认为现在游行是个好主意。

sentences.en: And why don't you think it's a good idea?
sentences.zh: 为什么你认为这不是个好主意？

sentences.en: To me, it kind of feels like trying to recreate something that should never be recreated or should have never had to have been recreated.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这感觉就像试图重现一些永远不该被重现，或者永远不应该需要被重现的东西。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Have you ever, this is probably a stupid analogy, but let me just bring it up.
sentences.zh: 你有没有，这可能是一个愚蠢的类比，但让我提一下。

sentences.en: Have you ever gone to a restaurant with your partner and had, like, the best meal?
sentences.zh: 你有没有和你的伴侣去过一家餐馆，吃过最棒的一顿饭？

sentences.en: And then you go back and it's like, it sucked.
sentences.zh: 然后你再去的时候，感觉，糟透了。

sentences.en: That's kind of the way I feel about the Women's March right now.
sentences.zh: 我现在对“妇女大游行”的感觉差不多就是这样。

sentences.en: It's like, I can never recreate for me what that moment was in history and in my life.
sentences.zh: 就好像，我再也无法重现那个时刻在我生命中和历史上的意义了。

sentences.en: And I don't want to.
sentences.zh: 我也不想重现。

sentences.en: And now, now I'm going to just do something else.
sentences.zh: 现在，我现在打算做点别的。

sentences.en: I'm going more, a little more inward.
sentences.zh: 我打算更多地向内探索，稍微向内一点。

sentences.en: So that, yeah, I guess I'm, I guess I'm trying a different restaurant.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我想我是在尝试换一家餐厅。

sentences.en: There needs to be some time to reflect and regroup and really look at ourselves and say, what are we doing wrong?
sentences.zh: 我们需要一些时间来反思、重整旗鼓，真正审视自己，问问我们哪里做错了？

sentences.en: Like, where do we go from here?
sentences.zh: 比如，接下来我们该往哪里走？

sentences.en: And what, what do you plan on doing instead?
sentences.zh: 那你打算做什么来代替呢？

sentences.en: I mean, that's really hard.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这真的很难。

sentences.en: That is the question, right?
sentences.zh: 这才是关键问题，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, well, what do you do?
sentences.zh: 比如，好吧，你该做什么呢？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: But the answer is probably not right before us.
sentences.zh: 但答案可能并不就在我们眼前。

sentences.en: If we jump to the conclusion right away and say, okay, well, then we need to do X, Y, and Z.
sentences.zh: 如果我们立刻跳到结论，说，好吧，那我们需要做甲、乙、丙。

sentences.en: Maybe, like, are we not doing a disservice to the lesson that we should learn from this?
sentences.zh: 也许，我们是不是辜负了我们本应从中吸取的教训？

sentences.en: Like, maybe we need to be more thoughtful about it and examine how we may have played a role in it.
sentences.zh: 也许我们需要更深思熟虑一些，审视一下我们自己可能在其中扮演了什么角色。

sentences.en: So it's the time to reflect and regroup, but it's not the time to march.
sentences.zh: 所以现在是反思和重整旗鼓的时候，但不是游行的时候。

sentences.en: I don't think that marching will do us any good.
sentences.zh: 我不认为游行对我们有什么好处。

sentences.en: That's not the direction we should go in.
sentences.zh: 那不是我们应该前进的方向。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: On Monday, President-elect Donald Trump confirmed that he intends to declare a national emergency and use the U.S.
sentences.zh: 周一，当选总统唐纳德·特朗普证实，他打算宣布国家进入紧急状态，并动用美国

sentences.en: military in some form to assist in his plans for mass deportations of undocumented immigrants.
sentences.zh: 军队以某种形式协助他实施大规模驱逐无证移民的计划。

sentences.en: Trump was responding to a post made by the head of the conservative group, Judicial Watch, that said Trump's administration would, quote,
sentences.zh: 特朗普是在回应保守派组织“司法观察”负责人发布的一篇帖子，该帖子称特朗普政府将，引用：

sentences.en: declare a national emergency and use military assets to address illegal immigration through a mass deportation program.
sentences.zh: 宣布国家进入紧急状态，并动用军事资产，通过大规模驱逐计划来解决非法移民问题。

sentences.en: On his social media platform, Truth Social, Trump responded with the comment, true.
sentences.zh: 在他的社交媒体平台“真实社交”上，特朗普回应称：真的。

sentences.en: Congress has granted presidents broad power to declare national emergencies at their discretion.
sentences.zh: 国会已授予总统广泛的权力，可自行决定宣布国家进入紧急状态。

sentences.en: And Trump nominated Sean Duffy, a former Republican congressman from Wisconsin and Fox business host,
sentences.zh: 此外，特朗普提名了肖恩·达菲，他是威斯康星州前共和党众议员，也是福克斯商业频道的节目主持人，

sentences.en: and whose wife, Rachel Campos Duffy, is a Fox News host as his choice to lead the Transportation Department.
sentences.zh: 他的妻子瑞秋·坎波斯·达菲是福克斯新闻频道的主持人，特朗普选择他来领导交通部。

sentences.en: Trump continued to deliberate over candidates for several high-level positions, including Treasury Secretary, a post that will be crucial to his economic agenda.
sentences.zh: 特朗普继续斟酌几个高级职位的候选人，包括财政部长，这个职位对他实现经济议程至关重要。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Lindsay Garrison, with help from Sidney Harper and Eric Krupke.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由琳赛·加里森制作，西德尼·哈珀和埃里克·克鲁普克提供协助。

sentences.en: It was edited by Devin Taylor, Ben Calhoun, and Lexi Diao.
sentences.zh: 由德文·泰勒、本·卡尔霍恩和莱克西·迪奥剪辑。

sentences.en: Research assistance by Susan Lee contains original music by Dan Powell,
sentences.zh: 苏珊·李提供研究协助，包含丹·鲍威尔创作的原创音乐，

sentences.en: Rowan Nemisto, Elisheba Etoop, and Marian Lozano, and was engineered by Chris Wood.

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是今天的《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 选举迎来了一群自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《地铁》节目中，我和萨拉·凯尼格将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《地铁》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 在任何你收听播客的地方都可以收听。
